title: Multilingual Large Language Models do not comprehend all natural languages to equal degrees

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM performance on a short-scenario language comprehension benchmark (Yes-No questions) adapted from English into 11 other typologically diverse languages, measuring accuracy and stability across repetitions compared to human baselines.
Modeling model comprehension accuracy and stability as a function of language size (total number of speakers, acting as a proxy for high-resource vs. low-resource data availability).
Analyzing the interaction between language size and writing system by comparing model performance on Latin-based scripts versus non-Latin-based scripts.

Balancing the evaluated languages to compare performance between 6 languages predominantly associated with WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialised, Rich, and Democratic) communities and 6 languages associated with non-WEIRD communities.
